title: gemm_bias's mixed_magnitude tolerance is met by no fp32 accumulation order at all, only by accumulating in fp64, so the task cannot qualify on any target

evidence.retained: bw1100 /home/testuser01/oci-dcu-runs/gemm_bias-20260918-064243, four turns and a 400000 token budget, adhered with endpoint_observation no_qualified_candidate; and a CPU-only reproduction at the launcher's shape for this task (M=128, K=256, N=1024) using the Workload's own generator and its own reference_outputs oracle, every accumulator's dtype asserted rather than assumed
sites: that run's correctness_output: participants.baseline.preflight.launches -- mixed_magnitude passed false, max_abs_error 0.09375, output_mismatches 27, while primary, zeros, near_zero and alternating all pass
the same document's candidate half fails the same case with the same 0.09375; the run's pooled output_mismatches is 54, 27 from each participant

the declared tolerance_rationale, verbatim: sized from the measured worst sequential-FP32 departure from an fsum oracle, '3.1e-2 absolute at outputs of order 2e5', and 'It is a numerical allowance, not device calibration'

the oracle is declared real_gemm_bias_fsum_then_fp32: exact fp32 products summed by math.fsum without intermediate rounding, plus bias, rounded once to fp32 (src/open_cake_ir/tasks/gemm/workload.py:79 and :162). reference_outputs returns a float64 container whose every value is exactly fp32-representable, which is what a reader checking the dtype alone will get wrong

measured on CPU against that oracle, every accumulator fp32: sequential 0.09375 with 27 elements outside tolerance, a plain fp32 matmul the same, split-K at widths 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 between 0.0625 and 0.09375 with 16 to 26 outside; accumulating in fp64 and rounding once departs by 0 with none outside

the 27 elements sequential fp32 fails have |ref| between 2.67627 and 102.895, median 21.3013, deviations 0.00201511 to 0.0186691 against allowances 0.00126763 to 0.0112895 -- cancellation survivors, not the large outputs
the same measurement on the primary case: every ordering passes

observation:
The starter reference does not pass the Workload's own validation set. mixed_magnitude is the case it fails -- signed powers of two from 2^-12 to 2^8, so a contraction over K accumulates terms spanning twenty binades -- and it fails by 0.09375 on 27 elements while the other four cases pass. Two turns produced two different candidate digests and both were rejected on correctness with the identical error, which is the tell that the error is not the candidate's: Common Evaluation checks both participants against the oracle, so a candidate is compared against a reference the baseline cannot match either.

This record's measurement has been wrong twice and the corrections are part of it. The first version claimed the tolerance was met by strictly sequential fp32 and concluded it 'bounds the one order nothing uses'; its probe built the sequential accumulator from a float64 array and so accumulated in fp64. The second held every accumulator in fp32 but compared them against an unrounded fp64 matmul of its own rather than against reference_outputs -- a rounding mismatch of the same family as the one it was correcting -- and reported figures (0.0855395, 0.0596697, 21, 22) that reproduce nothing. Both were caught by an independent reviewer reproducing the measurement rather than reading it.

Measured against the Workload's own oracle -- fsum-exact then rounded once to fp32, not the fp64 an earlier version of this sentence called it, which is a third rounding description this record has had to correct: sequential fp32 departs by 0.09375 with 27 elements outside tolerance -- the baseline's observed failure, to the digit. A plain fp32 matmul is identical. Split-K at six widths departs between 0.0625 and 0.09375 with 16 to 26 outside. Accumulating in fp64 and rounding once departs by 0 with none outside: with this case's dyadic inputs a 256-term fp64 dot is exact, so rounding it to fp32 lands on the same fp32 value the fsum oracle rounds to -- it equals the oracle rather than merely passing.

So no fp32 accumulation order meets this case's elementwise tolerance, and the one thing that does is the oracle's own arithmetic. The task cannot qualify on gfx938, on sm_103a, or on anything else contracting in fp32; that it was also reported failing on B300 needs no separate cause.

Where the failures sit matters for the fix. They are not the large outputs: the 27 elements have |ref| between 2.68 and 102.9 with a median of 21.3, deviations between 0.002 and 0.019 against allowances between 0.0013 and 0.0113. They are elements where twenty binades of signed terms cancelled down to something small, so an absolute error formed at full magnitude survives while rtol, scaled to the small result, buys almost nothing. The rationale's '3.1e-2 absolute at outputs of order 2e5' describes a magnitude that is comfortably inside tolerance here.
proposed_change:
The Workload Contract owns this. Re-deriving the allowance across blocked and split-K orders would change nothing: sequential fp32 fails by as much as any of them, so the allowance is not mis-sized against the wrong order but below what fp32 delivers on this case at all.

Two shapes remain and the choice is the owner's. Narrow mixed_magnitude's exponent range so fewer terms cancel, which is what produces the surviving absolute error; or state the accumulation precision the case requires, since fp64 accumulation meets the allowance exactly and no fp32 order does. The rationale should then describe where the case fails -- cancellation survivors of order 10 -- rather than outputs of order 2e5, which pass.

Still do not widen atol to make the case pass. The number to change is the one whose derivation is wrong, and changing it means redoing that derivation against fp32 arithmetic and against the oracle the harness actually compares to.

No second target is needed: the reproduction is CPU-only and hardware-independent.
